title: All things work together (Romans 8:28)
hookLine: to them that love God all things work together unto good

cards: It's printed on mugs and greeting cards, and said at funerals, sometimes kindly, sometimes too fast: everything happens for a reason. It's usually meant well. On a terrible day, it can land like a slap.

Some who say it think they're quoting the Bible. So it's worth looking carefully at the verse it's often borrowed from, because what Paul actually says is both stronger and more careful than the greeting card.

teach.b: Here's the verse, in the Douay-Rheims: "And we know that to them that love God, all things work together unto good, to such as, according to his purpose, are called to be saints." First, what it doesn't say.
It doesn't say all things are good. Paul has just been talking about groaning, suffering, a creation in labor pains. In the next verses he'll list tribulation, famine, the sword.
He knows terrible things are terrible.

teach.h: GOD IS THE ONE WHO WEAVES.
teach.b: The Greek is sunergei. Not each thing good on its own, but all things, woven together, made to serve good. Third, who's doing the weaving.
The good isn't automatic, like fate. It comes from someone: the God whose Spirit, Paul said two verses earlier, prays in us. Fourth, the good Paul means is bigger than comfort.
The next verse says it plainly: to be conformed to the image of his Son.

teach.h: ALL THINGS WORK TOGETHER UNTO GOOD.
teach.b: Paul doesn't offer the verse as an explanation of why the bad thing happened, and he never says the reason will be visible. He says, we know.

how: Catholics speak of divine providence, God's care that guides all things toward good without causing evil, and some offer up their sufferings, uniting them with Christ's, trusting God to bring good from them.

p: being conformed to the image of his Son
the ones all things work together for

s: Romans 8:28 says that all things are good
it says all things work together for good. Paul knows hard things are hard.
Paul says we know all things work together, not that we will see how
the verse says we know. it never promises the reason will be visible.
the good Paul means is mainly comfort
the next verse names it: being conformed to the image of his Son.

games.q: a grieving friend is told everything happens for a reason. you're asked what Romans 8:28 really says. what do you say?
o: that God caused this for a reason.
that God works even in this toward good, though we may not see how.
that it isn't really so bad.
games.why: the verse doesn't call the bad thing good. it says God works all things together toward good for those who love him.

practice: Choose a setback from your past, not your deepest wound, just something that went wrong: a job you didn't get, a move you didn't want, a plan that fell apart.

Look at it from here and ask whether anything was woven out of it, a friendship, a strength, a direction you wouldn't have found; if so, be grateful, and if not, that's honest too, since Paul says we know, not that we see.
If you pray, hand God what you can't make sense of yet.

wordCard.voice: Sunergei. Paul's word, works together: not everything is good alone, but God weaves all things toward good for those who love him. Today's word.

carryVoice: Your line: all things. Not all things good, but all things woven toward good. Until tomorrow.

sources.q: And we know that to them that love God, all things work together unto good, to such as, according to his purpose, are called to be saints.
